description: Generator parameters for the synthetic benchmark (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2). Every parameter has a value, a source and a confidence level (§2.4). 'varied' parameters are swept in the sensitivity runs over 'range'; 'value' is the default run. Parameters without a source are marked confidence 'none' and are always varied.

people.source: Derived, not chosen (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.1): sample_size.minimum_people() with the generated world's REALISED minor share (44.4%) and family size (3.49 people, design effect 1.75) gives 31,104 (binding: minors' precision >= 0.999), rounded up. The 26 Oct assumptions (50% minors, 3 per family) gave 25,300 -> 26,000. The generator re-checks its own size on every run (summary.size_check). Gate G4 open: recalculated once the tolerances are agreed

origin_shares.source: BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.1: equal thirds so every origin reaches its slice minimum; results re-weighted to Dzaleka's mix afterwards

two_parent_share.source: none found; women and children are 93% of Dzaleka's population (situation research), so many households have one parent present

children_per_family.source: none found for Dzaleka; chosen so that families average about 3 people and about half of all people are under 18 (BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.1). The realised shares are reported by the generator

mother_age_at_first_child.source: none found for the corridor; uniform range chosen for plausibility

birth_spacing_years.source: none found for the corridor; uniform range chosen for plausibility

parent_birth_years.source: Tuned 16 Nov 2026 with older_household_share so that minors are close to half (realised 44.5%) and people aged 50+ are a real slice (6.7%); BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.1. No corridor source

rw_father_element_q.source: Conflicting: HRW 1999 (most Rwandans do not share a family name) vs The New Times, 6 May 2026 (children traditionally take the father's surname); BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.2

bi_son_father_name_p.source: Disputed patronymic practice: Univ. of Burundi / Bigangara (1982) [B5]; BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md §2.2

cd_parent_nom_t.source: DRC Family Code arts 56-62 allow passing a parent's nom with at least one different element; how often is unknown

rw_names_per_person.source: Profile rw-nec-2026.1, structure.names_per_person (NEC district council candidates)

cd_token_count.source: Profile cd-congonames-2026.1, structure.token_count_distribution (5+ tokens, 0.25%, folded into 4)

young_child_birth_year.source: Children born from this year draw their Kinyarwanda/Kirundi name from the newborn profiles (rw-nisr-2026.1; bi-derived-2026.1, low confidence), older people from the adult profiles

older_household_share.source: none found; added (16 Nov 2026) so that older adults, who have lower literacy and are more often written by ear (RESEARCH_LOG.md, 28 Oct), form a real slice

older_parent_birth_years.source: CENI 2025 profile birth decades start in the 1940s-1950s; range for older households

invention.rule: A slot whose element is not drawn from a profile's listed (5+ times) elements is filled with an INVENTED element: a character-trigram chain trained on that slot's listed elements, rejected if it equals a listed element. The invention share per slot is the profile's uncovered share: 1 - (sum of listed counts / records). Christian given names are a closed set and are never invented: their uncovered share is drawn from the corridor-wide pool of listed Christian names of the same sex (all three profiles).
